findings.summary: security.gates.spec_gate is a second source of truth that silently overrides an explicit spec.strictness: block
findings.suggestion: Derive severity from resolve_strictness; render the legacy key from strictness so they cannot disagree.

findings.summary: STRICTNESS_EXEMPT documents one exception while a second de-facto strictness reader (the severity key) existed undocumented
findings.suggestion: Fold the legacy key into strictness or document it as an exception.

findings.summary: _ADVISED_DEV_MODE_PATHS repeats the non-atomic check-then-act memo pattern; no multi-threaded caller exists today
findings.suggestion: Guard both memo sets with one lock if a threaded caller ever appears.

findings.summary: the strictness render-drift signal reads harness.yaml and wrapup.md as two unlocked reads; a concurrent re-render can produce a transient false stale-render advisory
findings.suggestion: Accept (advisory-only, self-correcting) or read both under one snapshot.

findings.summary: the AST singleton scan misses .update(), .pop(), |= and keyword .get(key=...), so a second real writer passes green
findings.suggestion: Scan those spellings too; keep the accepted-limitations list honest.

findings.summary: the deleted plan-vs-verify drift signal has no test proving its state is now unreachable
findings.suggestion: Assert that no plan command renders at all.

findings.summary: block does not reliably block the spec gate: the retired preset-coupled security setting overrides the new single knob
findings.suggestion: Make the gate's allow/severity decision follow resolved strictness.

findings.summary: SPEC enforcement remains coupled to preset instead of the new strictness knob (find-unbound and judgment binding branch on preset)
findings.suggestion: Either move those gates to strictness or stop claiming warn blocks on nothing.

findings.summary: the documented CI strictness override is parsed but never forwarded to the CLI
